original_test_intent: Verify the approved Mellanox CX7 board can be safely removed and reinstalled in its mapped slot, is mechanically retained and fully seated, and returns with correct PCIe/HCA/network function and no new errors.
original_method: Record board FRU/serial/firmware and PCIe slot/topology/link baseline; quiesce workloads, shut down, remove AC and discharge; qualified ESD operator releases cables/retention and removes/reinstalls board per vendor sequence; inspect contacts/slot/bracket/latch and photograph seating; reconnect, power on, verify PCIe width/rate, HCA identity/firmware, network link and error/log delta; restore configuration.
manual_activity: Qualified hardware operator removes and reinstalls the exact CX7 board under powered-down ESD procedure; agent may collect pre/post digital evidence.
required_inputs: CX7 FRU/serial/firmware and PCIe slot/riser/topology map
Vendor power-down/discharge, cable, latch and retention procedure
Cycle count, seating/torque/inspection criteria and recovery plan
Expected PCIe width/rate, HCA/network identity/link and error tolerances
safety_requirements: Quiesce workloads, shut down, remove AC and verify discharge
Use ESD protection and qualified handling of board/slot/cables
Stop on damaged contacts/slot/bracket, excessive force or wrong topology
Do not power on before retention/cabling check or retry a failed reseat blindly
agent_execution_scope: Collect pre/post PCIe/HCA/network/firmware and error evidence
Correlate operator photos and service timestamps
Do not handle hardware, approve hot removal, infer seating solely from enumeration, retry or decide verdict
engineer_actions: Approve board/slot identity and service procedure
Approve mechanical seating/retention criteria and cycle count
Approve PCIe/HCA/link/error recovery oracle and final state
Review evidence and decide PASS, FAIL, or BLOCKED

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: Software cannot exercise board removal or prove bracket/latch/contact seating; it only validates post-service function.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Compare exact board FRU and PCIe topology/link capabilities, HCA health and network/errors before and after manual reinstall.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: Board plug cycle, proper seating and error-free redetection remain.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Use powered-down documented service with FRU/slot photo traceability and topology-aware post-boot validation.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds electrical isolation, board/slot identity, retention/cable inspection and complete function comparison.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: A device can enumerate with degraded PCIe width, wrong slot mapping, missing ports or new correctable errors.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Board extraction can damage contacts/riser, disturb adjacent cables and change firmware/network naming; rollback requires controlled teardown, not immediate repeat.

project_override_considerations: If the CX7 is not field-replaceable or the platform uses liquid/thermal attachments, obtain the specialized vendor procedure and resources before execution.
expected_evidence: Pre/post PCIe width/rate, HCA/network/link and error/log diff

engineering_decision_pending.question: Resolve Functionality row 2269 Wistron-HW-00025-V003: approve CX7 board FRU/serial/firmware, PCIe slot/riser/topology and attached cable map; vendor shutdown/AC removal/discharge, latch/retention/torque and reinstall sequence, cycle count and objective contact/slot/bracket seating criteria; define expected PCIe width/rate, HCA/network identity/link, error counters/logs, rollback and final configuration.

review_improvement: Preserves the board plug-cycle coverage while elevating it from subjective handling to controlled critical service with topology-aware recovery evidence.
independent_technical_reasoning: Removing a PCIe/HCA board affects high-speed contacts, auxiliary cabling, retention and system topology. Successful enumeration is not enough: marginal seating may train fewer lanes or accumulate correctable errors, and reinstall can alter interface naming or cable mapping. A safe review must therefore require full de-energization, exact FRU/slot identity, mechanical inspection and pre/post lane, device, link and error evidence before declaring the service path acceptable.
